blocks.name: boiler
blocks.notes: Meets the remaining hot-water demand with the boiler.

blocks.name: chiller
blocks.notes: Meets the remaining chilled-water demand with the chiller.

blocks.name: pump_zero
blocks.notes: Stops both loop pumps when their CDL enable is false.

blocks.name: pump_start_threshold
blocks.notes: Requires more than 0.5 kW of load before enabling a loop.

blocks.name: hot_water_pump_needed
blocks.notes: Enables hot-water circulation from the measured heating request.

blocks.name: chilled_water_pump_needed
blocks.notes: Enables chilled-water circulation from the measured cooling request.

blocks.notes: Selects the hot-water pump command from its CDL enable.

blocks.name: chilled_water_pump_select

blocks.name: hot_water_supply_setpoint
blocks.notes: Commands a 45 °C hot-water supply temperature until a reset sequence is added.

blocks.name: chilled_water_supply_setpoint
blocks.notes: Commands a 7 °C chilled-water supply temperature until a reset sequence is added.

blocks.name: source_zero
blocks.notes: Minimum heat or cooling production command is zero kilowatts.

blocks.name: hot_water_source_error
blocks.notes: Hot-water supply target minus measured temperature.

blocks.name: chilled_water_source_error
blocks.notes: Measured chilled-water supply temperature minus its target.

blocks.name: hot_water_source_gain
blocks.notes: Corrects hot-water production by 6 kW per kelvin of supply error; editable for the 5,000 kg volume.

blocks.name: chilled_water_source_gain
blocks.notes: Corrects chilled-water production by 6 kW per kelvin of supply error; editable for the 5,000 kg volume.

blocks.name: hot_water_source_sum
blocks.notes: Adds hot-water temperature correction to the predicted heating load.

blocks.name: chilled_water_source_sum
blocks.notes: Adds chilled-water temperature correction to the predicted cooling load.

blocks.name: hot_water_source_nonnegative
blocks.notes: Prevents a negative hot-water source production command.

blocks.name: chilled_water_source_nonnegative
blocks.notes: Prevents a negative chilled-water source production command.

blocks.name: heat_pump_hot_eligible
blocks.notes: Offer hot-water demand to dispatch only after measured hot-water flow is proven.

blocks.name: heat_pump_chilled_eligible
blocks.notes: Offer chilled-water demand to dispatch only after measured chilled-water flow is proven.

blocks.name: heat_pump_utilization_limit
blocks.notes: Editable fraction of available equipment capacity offered to the heat pump. Legacy dispatch tuning migrates here; it no longer splits every demand by a fixed share.

blocks.name: heat_pump_zero_capacity
blocks.notes: Do not offer negative heat-pump capacity.

blocks.name: heat_pump_capacity_nonnegative
blocks.notes: Clamp edited utilization at zero.

blocks.name: heat_pump_capacity_limited
blocks.notes: Never offer more than physical available capacity.

blocks.name: heat_pump_total_load
blocks.notes: Total hot and chilled source demand.

blocks.name: heat_pump_divisor_floor
blocks.notes: Avoid division by zero when the plant is idle.

blocks.name: heat_pump_safe_total
blocks.notes: Positive denominator for allocation.

blocks.name: heat_pump_capacity_ratio
blocks.notes: Available capacity divided by total demand.

blocks.name: heat_pump_full_fraction
blocks.notes: Do not command above either water-loop demand.

blocks.name: heat_pump_allocated_fraction
blocks.notes: Share of each load served by the heat pump within combined capacity.

blocks.name: boiler_residual
blocks.notes: Boiler serves the hot-water load left after heat-pump allocation.

blocks.name: chiller_residual
blocks.notes: Chiller serves the chilled-water load left after heat-pump allocation.

blocks.name: heat_pump_mode_threshold
blocks.notes: Ignore negligible loads when identifying operating mode.

blocks.name: heat_pump_cooling_requested

Shared four-pipe plant: the heat pump serves a configurable fraction of heating and cooling demand; boiler and chiller cover the remainder. Equipment-specific CDL allocation shares available heat-pump capacity across hot and chilled demand and commands boiler/chiller for the residual. The physical simulator approximates simultaneous compressor energy without a calibrated refrigerant model. The G36 sample aggregates AHU chilled-water requests and resets the supply target every five minutes. AHU hot-water requests reset the supply target every five minutes between 44 and 50 °C. Persistent VAV reheat demand contributes requests to the hot-water reset. AHU Stage 1 freeze protection contributes hot-water reset requests. Stage 3 freeze shutdown energizes chilled-water pumping. Measured loop water flow and graph pump enable prove source operation before heat-pump, boiler, or chiller commands are issued. CDL detects heat-pump and backup source-stage changes, then holds both sampled water resets until measured flow and the selected stage remain stable for 900 seconds. Sampled reset values set remote hot/chilled differential-pressure targets; editable CDL PI loops use measured pressure to command pump speed. Raw equipment-availability inputs gate heat-pump capacity and backup source commands in CDL. Sampled water-reset holds now require raw source running status as well as water-flow proof. An editable timed CDL fault latch removes heat-pump capacity after a failed start; operator reset permits another attempt. An editable timed CDL fault latch inhibits boiler after a failed start until operator reset. An editable timed CDL fault latch inhibits chiller after a failed start until operator reset.

Serves five VAV zones. Outdoor temperature chooses the supply-air target. Measured mixed and supply temperatures drive editable heating and cooling coil valve loops; total airflow request sets fan speed. An editable mixed-air PI loop modulates outdoor air when temperature conditions permit free cooling; minimum outside-air flow has priority. VAV cooling requests reset the sampled supply-air target within its outdoor-temperature bound. A timed Stage 1 freeze response reduces outdoor air to its minimum and sends two hot-water requests. Stage 2 closes outdoor air for one hour and reports a Level 3 ventilation alarm. Stage 3 latches fan shutdown, outdoor-air closure, full cooling-coil opening, and heating protection until a safe operator reset. Differential dry-bulb hysteresis, raw fan proof, and all freeze stages qualify economizer operation. Occupied mode and fan proof gate the measured-flow minimum; fan request permits normal economizer air in cooldown and preconditioning. An editable mechanical maximum limits final outdoor-damper travel. The return damper has an independent command and mechanical maximum. Its minimum-OA limit closes return air as PI demand rises above 0.5. The mixer derives outside-air share from both actuator openings. The first half of minimum-OA PI output opens the outdoor damper from zero to full stroke; the second half limits return-damper opening. Editable zone area/population components, measured primary flow, zone outdoor fractions, and system ventilation efficiency determine the minimum outside-air setpoint. Supply fan command/status alarms use editable 15-second start and 60-second stop delays. Measured fan speed feeds an editable five-minute drive speed tracking diagnostic. Physical outdoor and return damper position sensors feed editable CDL tracking alarms. A CDL ten-minute high-limit state hold reduces economizer mode cycling; fan and freeze safety gates remain immediate. A CDL switch selects fixed or differential dry-bulb economizer high limit. CDL delays outdoor-air closure 15 seconds and holds the return damper fully open 180 seconds after economizer disable.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_on

blocks.notes: Stage 1 clears after supply air stays above 7 °C for five minutes.

blocks.notes: Detect low measured supply-air temperature.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_warm
blocks.notes: Detect recovered measured supply-air temperature.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_on_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes below the Stage 1 temperature threshold.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_off_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes above the recovery threshold.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_latch
blocks.notes: Hold Stage 1 during the supply-temperature recovery interval.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_outdoor_air
blocks.notes: Override the outdoor-air command to its editable minimum while Stage 1 is active.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_request_integer
blocks.notes: Convert Stage 1 status into a hot-water plant request.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_one_two_requests

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_on
blocks.notes: Stage 2 begins after supply air stays below 3.3 °C for five minutes.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_cold
blocks.notes: Detect the deeper measured supply-air temperature fault.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_on_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes below the Stage 2 temperature threshold.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_latch
blocks.notes: Hold the outdoor-air interruption until its one-hour timer has elapsed.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_to_integer
blocks.notes: Convert Stage 2 status for a sampled timer feedback path.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_to_real
blocks.notes: Convert the sampled Stage 2 status to a Real signal for the duration comparison.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_previous
blocks.notes: Break the Stage 2 latch/timer feedback loop using its prior sampled status.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_zero
blocks.notes: Zero means the prior Stage 2 state was inactive.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_previous_active
blocks.notes: Was Stage 2 active at the prior sample?

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_hour
blocks.notes: Clear Stage 2 after one hour including the sampled feedback and timer step.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_closed
blocks.notes: Close all outdoor-air paths while minimum ventilation is interrupted.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_outdoor_air
blocks.notes: Close outdoor air during Stage 2; otherwise restore Stage 1 or normal control.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_alarm_integer

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_alarm_double
blocks.notes: Build Level 2 from the active Stage 2 alarm bit.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_two_alarm_three

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_fifteen_threshold
blocks.notes: A supply temperature below 3.3 °C for 15 minutes requires shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_five_threshold
blocks.notes: A supply temperature below 1 °C for five minutes requires shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_below_fifteen
blocks.notes: Detect the sustained 3.3 °C shutdown fault.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_below_five
blocks.notes: Detect the deeper 1 °C shutdown fault.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_fifteen_delay
blocks.notes: Require 15 continuous minutes below 3.3 °C.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_five_delay
blocks.notes: Require five continuous minutes below 1 °C.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_sensor_fault
blocks.notes: Either sustained low-temperature condition requires shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_trip
blocks.notes: A freeze-stat trip or low-temperature fault requires shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_reset_temperature

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_reset_warm
blocks.notes: Supply air is warm enough to reset.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_stat_normal
blocks.notes: A freeze-stat trip must clear before operator reset.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_reset_safe
blocks.notes: Both supply temperature and freeze-stat status permit reset.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_reset_allowed
blocks.notes: Accept an operator reset only when the fault has cleared.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_latch

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_fan_off
blocks.notes: Stop the supply fan during shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_fan
blocks.notes: Override the graph fan command to zero.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_outdoor_closed
blocks.notes: Close outdoor air during shutdown.

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_outdoor_air

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_cooling_valve

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_heating_target

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_heating_pi

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_heating_valve

blocks.name: freeze_stage_three_alarm_two

Serves five VAV zones. Outdoor temperature chooses the supply-air target. Measured mixed and supply temperatures drive editable heating and cooling coil valve loops; total airflow request sets fan speed. An editable mixed-air PI loop modulates outdoor air when temperature conditions permit free cooling; minimum outside-air flow has priority. VAV cooling requests reset the sampled supply-air target within its outdoor-temperature bound. A timed Stage 1 freeze response reduces outdoor air to its minimum and sends two hot-water requests. Stage 2 closes outdoor air for one hour and reports a Level 3 ventilation alarm. Stage 3 latches fan shutdown, outdoor-air closure, full cooling-coil opening, and heating protection until a safe operator reset. Differential dry-bulb hysteresis, raw fan proof, and all freeze stages qualify economizer operation. Occupied mode and fan proof gate the measured-flow minimum; fan request permits normal economizer air in cooldown and preconditioning. An editable mechanical maximum limits final outdoor-damper travel. The return damper has an independent command and mechanical maximum. Its minimum-OA limit closes return air as PI demand rises above 0.5. The mixer derives outside-air share from both actuator openings. The first half of minimum-OA PI output opens the outdoor damper from zero to full stroke; the second half limits return-damper opening. Editable zone area/population components, measured primary flow, zone outdoor fractions, and system ventilation efficiency determine the minimum outside-air setpoint. Supply fan command/status alarms use editable 15-second start and 60-second stop delays. Measured fan speed feeds an editable five-minute drive speed tracking diagnostic. Physical outdoor and return damper position sensors feed editable CDL tracking alarms. A CDL ten-minute high-limit state hold reduces economizer mode cycling; fan and freeze safety gates remain immediate. A CDL switch selects fixed or differential dry-bulb economizer high limit. CDL delays outdoor-air closure 15 seconds and holds the return damper fully open 180 seconds after economizer disable.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

The scheduled mode uses occupied 21/24 °C setpoints. Five minutes without a person widens both setpoints by 0.5 K and reduces ventilation minimums; one minute of presence restores them. Outside the occupied schedule, shared group setback and setup modes enable editable 18/32 °C targets; otherwise heating and cooling are off and ventilation minimum is zero. Before occupancy, warm-up or cooldown restores occupied temperature setpoints but keeps the reduced ventilation minimum. Heating mode raises airflow above minimum only after the discharge is warm, while preconditioning can use the heating maximum. CDL TrueDelay and Latch blocks confirm arrival and vacancy from the raw occupancy sensor. Measured airflow and discharge temperature are fed back from the physical model. A CDL discharge-temperature reset and valve PI loop command reheat, and five-minute low-flow and high-discharge alarms report persistent faults. Heating demand resets the discharge target; a PI loop uses measured discharge temperature to command reheat. Heating airflow rises only after the discharge is 3 K warmer than the room. The damper PI tracks measured primary airflow; its setpoint remains separate from the physical delivery. Occupied presence gates editable area and population ventilation components; measured discharge selects heating or cooling distribution effectiveness. A cooling call can open its damper while supply air is warm during AHU startup; a warm supply is diagnosed at the AHU rather than suppressing the request. The local CDL mode distinguishes occupied, sensor standby, warm-up, cooldown, setup, setback, and unoccupied conditions; these teaching codes are not the G36 zone-group enumeration. Group warm-up and cooldown now come from the five-zone CDL coordinator; occupied setpoint edits feed its sampled optimal-start estimate. Unoccupied heating/cooling is commanded by the shared CDL group setback/setup/freeze decisions. Open windows disable ordinary terminal heating and cooling; group freeze setback retains heating. A timed local occupancy override selects occupied terminal mode and makes its AHU group occupied through CDL. Editable occupied-mode low-flow diagnosis waits for 30 minutes of AHU fan proof, then raises Level 3 below 70% or Level 2 below 50% of requested primary airflow after five minutes. A Level 3 airflow-sensor calibration alarm reports residual measured flow above ten percent of design after ten minutes of AHU fan-off proof. Occupied low-discharge alarms use measured temperature, physical heating production proof, an editable reset-importance suppressor, and ten-minute Level 3/2 delays. Editable Level 4 leakage alarms use fan status, closed damper command plus measured flow, and closed measured valve plus discharge temperature rise.

blocks.notes: Each closed-window zone samples its error at the start horizon. A CDL latch opens a recovery episode only after optimal start is requested, then holds observation into occupied operation. CDL samples the held recovery rate at midnight when the sampled horizon error calls for optimal start, and learns a three-day slope from measured setpoint attainment within fourteen hours, and uses the longest zone prediction. The editable seconds-per-kelvin constants initialize and bound the learned slopes. A sampled prior rate explicitly breaks the group feedback loop. Full G36 group mode coordination and reference-trace verification remain to be added.

blocks.notes: A positive occupied-setpoint error sampled at the start horizon qualifies the midnight moving-mean sample. Only measured setpoint attainment updates the held rate; open windows are excluded.

blocks.name: zero_error
blocks.notes: Only a positive occupied-setpoint error requires recovery.

blocks.notes: Ignore episodes with less than 0.5 K of initial error.

blocks.notes: A zone within 0.1 K of setpoint has recovered.

blocks.notes: Avoid division by a nearly zero recovery time.

blocks.name: zone_group_2
blocks.description: Five-zone CDL operating-mode coordinator for one AHU.
blocks.notes: Each closed-window zone samples its error at the start horizon. A CDL latch opens a recovery episode only after optimal start is requested, then holds observation into occupied operation. CDL samples the held recovery rate at midnight when the sampled horizon error calls for optimal start, and learns a three-day slope from measured setpoint attainment within fourteen hours, and uses the longest zone prediction. The editable seconds-per-kelvin constants initialize and bound the learned slopes. A sampled prior rate explicitly breaks the group feedback loop. Full G36 group mode coordination and reference-trace verification remain to be added.

notes: Compare this sample with FourPipeBuildingControls using the same weather, equipment, and physical model. Each zone has a debounced Brick occupancy sensor. Occupied setpoints are 21/24 °C, standby widens them by 0.5 K, and unoccupied setback/setup targets are 18/32 °C. Ventilation minimums and AHU fan minimums also reset. Qualified VAV cooling requests drive a sampled AHU supply-air temperature reset. Two five-zone CDL group controllers coordinate optimal start within three hours of occupancy, shared unoccupied setback/setup, and a zone freeze setback alarm. The AHUs use outdoor/return temperature comparisons and measured mixed-air feedback to modulate free cooling. Measured primary airflow and discharge temperature feed an editable terminal discharge setpoint and valve loop, plus editable measured-feedback terminal alarms. Timed Stage 1–3 AHU freeze protection overrides air delivery and requests water-side pumps; Stage 2 interrupts outdoor ventilation for one hour after a deeper fault, while Stage 3 latches shutdown. This is a G36-inspired subset; full G36 economizer limits, plant staging, alarms, and CO2 sequences are not modeled. Two five-zone CDL group controllers coordinate warm-up and cooldown using a three-hour cap and sampled VAV occupied setpoints. Two five-zone CDL group controllers now command latched setback, setup, and zone freeze setback. Raw window contacts feed editable CDL group exclusion and terminal conditioning gates. Local override button contacts feed editable two-hour CDL holds before zone/group occupancy and Level 4 window alarms. CDL per-zone recovery learners replace fixed-rate optimal-start predictions; Rust supplies only schedule time and measured zone temperatures. VAV low-airflow alarms are calculated from measured delivery in editable CDL. Fan-off airflow sensor calibration alarms are editable CDL and use physical motor status and flow feedback. VAV low-discharge alarms are calculated in editable CDL from measured temperatures and physical hot-water production proof. Physical VAV actuator positions and seat-leak behavior feed editable CDL terminal leakage alarms. Physical fan status remains a raw input; editable CDL decides fan discrepancy alarms. Supply fan drive speed feedback is physical; its tracking alarm is CDL. AHU intake physics uses measured damper positions; CDL diagnoses command mismatch. Economizer high-limit state holds are editable CDL, with separate immediate fan and freeze gates. Each AHU has an editable fixed versus differential dry-bulb high-limit choice. Economizer disable damper transitions follow editable CDL timers.
